name: Kelly Criterion (Optimal Bet Fraction)
description: Computes the Kelly fraction (b*p-(1-p))/b, the share of a bankroll to wager to maximize the long-run growth rate given win probability p and net odds b (profit per unit staked on a win). It balances edge against risk of loss.
notes: Odds b are net (b=1 means win one unit per unit staked, i.e. even money). A negative result means the bet has no edge and should not be taken; many practitioners bet a fraction of the Kelly value.

name: Kelly Fraction (Continuous Returns)
description: Gives the optimal fraction of wealth to allocate to a risky asset, (mu-r)/sigma^2, where mu is the asset's expected return, r the risk-free rate, and sigma its volatility. It maximizes long-run logarithmic growth of the portfolio.
notes: sigma is the standard deviation of returns and is squared in the denominator (the variance). All inputs should be over the same horizon; a value above 1 implies leverage beyond fully invested.

name: Kelly Criterion Optimal Fraction
description: Gives the Kelly-optimal fraction of bankroll to wager, computed as (b*p-(1-p))/b where b is the net odds and p the win probability. It maximizes the expected long-run logarithmic growth of capital.
notes: b and p must be positive with p between 0 and 1. A negative result means the bet has no edge and should be avoided; the numerator is the expected net return per unit staked.

name: Kelly Fraction for a Two-Outcome Bet with Loss Fraction
description: Gives the Kelly fraction when a win gains b and a loss loses a of the stake: f* = p/a − (1 − p)/b.
notes: Reduces to the classic (bp − q)/b when the whole stake is lost (a = 1).

name: Position Size from Risk per Trade
description: Gives how many units to buy so that hitting the stop loses a fixed fraction of the account.
notes: Risking 1 % of 50,000 with a 5-point stop allows 100 units.

name: Risk–Reward Ratio
description: Divides the potential gain to the target by the potential loss to the stop.
notes: Here 2.4 : 1.

name: Break-even Win Rate for a Reward–Risk Ratio
description: Gives the fraction of trades that must win to break even when winners earn rr times what losers lose.
notes: With 2 : 1 you break even winning one trade in three.

name: Trading Expectancy per Trade
description: Gives the average profit per trade from the win rate and average win and loss sizes.
notes: Positive expectancy is necessary but not sufficient; position sizing controls the risk of ruin.

name: Profit Factor

variables.label: Profit or loss of each trade

description: Divides gross profit by gross loss over a list of trades.
notes: Above about 1.5 is usually considered a robust system.

name: Win Rate from a Trade List

variables.label: Profit or loss of each trade

description: Gives the percentage of trades that made money.
notes: Read together with average win and loss; a low win rate can still be profitable.

name: Margin Required for a Leveraged Position
description: Gives the collateral needed to open a leveraged position.
notes: A 3.33 % margin (30 : 1) on a 110,000 position needs about 3,667.

name: FX Pip Value in Account Currency
description: Gives the money value of a one-pip move for a currency position.
notes: A standard lot (100,000 units) of EUR/USD is worth 10 USD per pip. For yen pairs the pip size is 0.01.

name: Implied Probability from Decimal Odds
description: Converts decimal (European) odds into the probability they imply.
notes: Odds of 2.5 imply 40 %. Bookmaker odds also include a margin, so the implied probabilities add up to more than 1.

name: American Odds to Decimal Odds
description: Converts American moneyline odds (+150 or −150) to decimal odds.
notes: −150 means stake 150 to win 100, i.e. decimal odds 1.667.

name: Fractional Odds to Decimal Odds
description: Converts British fractional odds a/b to decimal odds.
notes: 5/2 is 3.5 in decimal.

name: Bookmaker Margin (Overround)
description: Adds the implied probabilities of all outcomes of an event; the excess over 100 % is the bookmaker's margin.
notes: Lower margins mean better value for the bettor.

name: Fair Probability with the Margin Removed
description: Normalises implied probabilities so they add to 1 (proportional method), giving a margin-free estimate for one outcome.
notes: More refined methods (Shin, power) treat favourites and longshots differently.

name: Expected Value of a Bet
description: Gives the average profit of a bet from your own probability estimate and the offered odds.
notes: Positive only if p × odds > 1.

name: Kelly Stake for Decimal Odds
description: Gives the Kelly fraction of the bankroll to bet at decimal odds when you believe the win probability is p.
notes: Negative means do not bet. Many bettors use half-Kelly to reduce swings.

name: Arbitrage (Sure Bet) Check

variables.label: Best decimal odds for each outcome

description: Returns 1 when the best available odds on all outcomes imply probabilities adding to less than 1, so that backing every outcome guarantees a profit.
notes: Bookmakers often limit accounts that do this.

name: Impermanent Loss (Constant-Product AMM)
description: Gives the loss of a 50/50 liquidity position in a constant-product market maker (x·y = k) compared with simply holding, when the price ratio changes by k.
notes: A doubling of the price costs about 5.7 % against holding, before trading fees.

name: Constant-Product AMM Swap Output
description: Gives the tokens received for a swap in an x·y = k pool (Uniswap v2 style), after the pool fee.
notes: Larger trades get worse prices (price impact) because the curve bends.

name: Price Impact of an AMM Swap
description: Compares the average price of a swap with the pool's price before the trade.
notes: Includes the fee; about 1.28 % for a 1 % trade of the pool here.

name: Bitcoin Block Subsidy at a Block Height
description: Gives the new coins per block, which halves every 210,000 blocks (about four years).
notes: The fourth halving at block 840,000 (April 2024) cut it to 3.125 BTC.

name: Bitcoin Supply Issued up to a Block Height
description: Adds up all block subsidies up to a height.
notes: Supply approaches 21 million; 19.6875 million had been issued at block 840,000.

name: Expected Mining Revenue per Day
description: Estimates daily revenue from proof-of-work mining as your share of the network hash rate times the coins issued per day (144 blocks).
notes: Subtract electricity (power × hours × price) for profit.

name: Bid–Ask Spread (Percent of Mid)
description: Gives the quoted spread as a share of the mid price, a measure of trading cost and liquidity.
notes: A round trip costs about one full spread.

name: Risk of Ruin (Fixed Bet Size)

variables.label: Edge per bet (win prob − loss prob)

description: Gives the probability of eventually losing a bankroll of u units with even-money bets at a given edge.
notes: Doubling the bankroll squares the risk.
